## [b1] relayer: stable Hashi MessageDispatched pagination (issue #518)
project: vea
seam: relayer-cli/src/utils/hashiHelpers
deps: none
risk: medium
status: review
acceptance: |
  yarn workspace @kleros/vea-relayer-cli test passes; no MessageDispatched
  event can be skipped when a batch truncates a block.
description: |
  Envio Hashi pagination in `envioQueries.ts` uses blockNumber alone as the
  cursor; when one block holds more matching `MessageDispatched` events than
  the batch size, the checkpoint advances past that block and remaining
  same-block events are permanently skipped. Stable event-level pagination:
  cursor on (blockNumber, logIndex), or drain every matching event in the
  checkpoint block before advancing; checkpoint correct for full, partial and
  empty batches. Regression test: >10 matching events in one block, all
  processed across consecutive batches. Landed on `task/b1` as
  `a16f390` (review PASS; P2 notes: drain page-size assumption, unbounded
  drain loop cap).

## [b2] veashi-scanner: fail closed on partial VEA epoch detail (issue #514)

seam: veashi-scanner/lib/vea/client.ts, veashi-scanner/hooks/useVeaEpoch.ts
deps: none
risk: medium
status: review
acceptance: |
  yarn workspace @kleros/veashi-scanner build passes; failed gql vs valid-empty
  is distinguished; no partial epoch detail is returned on failure.
description: |
  `fetchEpochDetail` must distinguish a failed gql request from a valid empty
  message page and a valid empty relay batch, and propagate the indexer
  failure instead of returning partial message/relay data. `useVeaEpoch` must

  pagination normally. The package has no test framework — verification is the
  `tsc -b` build. Status: messages/relayed pagination fail-closed paths are
  already in the tree; the remaining gaps (snapshot query and claim query
  failures collapsing to valid-empty) were fixed and landed on `task/b2` as
  `02ed613` (review PASS; P2 nits: strict-null guards, misleading 'Not found'

## [validator-fix-1] arbToGnosis claimer must read the outbox with outbox-chain blocks (F1)
project: vea
seam: validator-cli/src/helpers/claimer.ts, validator-cli/src/utils/arbToEthState.ts, validator-cli/src/helpers/claimer.test.ts, validator-cli/src/utils/arbToEthState.test.ts
deps: none
risk: high
status: todo
acceptance: |
  yarn workspace @kleros/vea-validator-cli test passes; a new test with
  chainId 10200 and a distinct veaRouterProvider (Sepolia) + veaOutboxProvider
  (Chiado) proves makeClaim reads stateRoot / Claimed logs on the outbox's
  own chain, never with a Sepolia block number.
description: |
  Review finding F1: `checkAndClaim` sets `queryRpc = veaRouterProvider ??
  veaOutboxProvider`; for `arbToGnosis` the router is on Sepolia while the
  outbox is on Chiado, so `outboxBlock`, the lookback floor and
  `getBlock("finalized")` are Sepolia numbers applied to the Chiado
  `veaOutbox`. `findLatestLog` returns null and `makeClaim` silently never
  claims (no graph fallback reached). Fix: the outbox block/tag used for
  `stateRoot` and the `Claimed` scan must come from the **outbox's own
  provider** (`veaOutboxProvider`, Chiado); the router provider is only for
  Arbitrum→L1 finality/message status. Never substitute `queryRpc` for the
  outbox-chain provider. `arbToEth` behavior must be unchanged.

## [validator-fix-2] resolveSettledReadBlocks/getClaimResolveState: separate outbox-chain from L1 blocks (F2)
project: vea
seam: validator-cli/src/utils/arbToEthState.ts, validator-cli/src/helpers/validator.ts, validator-cli/src/utils/claim.ts, validator-cli/src/utils/arbToEthState.test.ts, validator-cli/src/utils/claim.test.ts

risk: high
status: todo
acceptance: |

  outbox chain (10200) != the L1 used for Arbitrum finality (11155111) proves
  outboxBlock is a Chiado block and claimHashes(epoch) is read with a Chiado
  blockTag on the Chiado outbox.
description: |
  Review finding F2: `resolveSettledReadBlocks` returns the L1 (Sepolia)
  finalized block as `outboxBlock`; for `arbToGnosis` the outbox chain is
  Chiado, so the docstring "finalized head on both chains" is false and
  `getClaimResolveState` applies a Sepolia block number to the Chiado
  `veaOutbox.claimHashes(epoch, { blockTag })`. Fix:
  `resolveSettledReadBlocks` must return the **outbox chain's** finalized
  block (a Chiado read for arbToGnosis), separately from the Sepolia block
  used for Arbitrum finality; `getClaimResolveState` needs both providers
  (outbox-chain + L1/router) passed explicitly rather than one conflated
  `queryRpc`.

## [validator-fix-3] getSentSnapshotData: parse args by route, not args[1] (F3)

description: |
  Review finding F3 (pre-existing, but blocks the resolve flow this branch
  rewrote): `sendSnapshot` signatures differ — arbToEth =
  `sendSnapshot(epoch, claim)`; arbToGnosis = `sendSnapshot(epoch, gasLimit,
  claim)`. `getSentSnapshotData` always parses `args[1]` as the claim, so for
  arbToGnosis the expectedClaimHash is garbage, `sendSnapshot.status` never
  becomes true and the challenger re-sends snapshots forever. Fix: select
  `args[1]` vs `args[2]` by inbox ABI/route (or parse by function fragment
  name).

## [validator-fix-4] Cold start: empty Claimed scan must trigger the indexer fallback (F4)

status: todo
acceptance: |

description: |
  Review finding F4: after > ~26 h downtime (or first start) there is no
  `Claimed` event inside the lookback window; the bounded `findLatestLog`
  returns null cleanly and `makeClaim` returns null **without** invoking the
  graph fallback, so the claimer silently stops claiming forever.
  `helpers/snapshot.ts` handles the identical "no log" case by throwing
  `NoMessageSavedError` to trigger the fallback; `claimer.ts` must do the
  same — treat `lastClaimLog == null` as "fall back to the indexer", never as
  "skip claiming".
